description: Catalog of mutants acknowledged as equivalent (semantically identical to the original code, so no test can kill them). Each entry is excluded from the per-file mutation-score denominator. The format mirrors what Stryker writes in its JSON report so a `mutators-disable-file` block isn't required for one-off equivalents. Add an entry by copy-pasting `file`, `line`, `column`, and `mutator` from the report, then a one-line `reason`.

entries.reason: `if (!db) { return local?.getArchiveRoute(...) }` is a fast-path for the no-DB case. The mutant `if (false)` skips this branch and falls through to `withSafeRouteRegistryFallback(... operation: () => db.prepare(...))`. When db is undefined the operation throws synchronously; withSafeRouteRegistryFallback catches and invokes the same `local.getArchiveRoute(normalizedPath)` fallback (or returns the same default `null` when no local registry is available). Observable result is identical for every (db, local-availability) pair.

Same equivalence class as L20:6 — replacing the if-body with `{}` removes the fast-path early return. Control falls through to withSafeRouteRegistryFallback which routes to the same local-registry fallback when db is undefined (catching the resulting `db.prepare` TypeError). Identical observable result.

`if (!db) { return local?.listSystemRoutes() ?? []; }` fast-path in listRuntimeSystemRoutes. Mutant `false` falls through to withSafeRouteRegistryFallback whose operation throws on `db.prepare` with undefined db; catch routes through the same local-registry fallback or the same `[]` default. Identical observable result.
Same equivalence class as L50:6 — empty if-body falls through to withSafeRouteRegistryFallback which catches the resulting TypeError and produces the same observable result.

`rows.map((row) => mapSystemRow(row)).filter(Boolean)` — the mutant drops `.filter(Boolean)`. mapSystemRow only returns `null` when its input row is itself null/undefined. The D1 `.all()` result.results never contains null/undefined entries — it returns a typed array of row objects. So mapSystemRow returns non-null for every element and the `.filter(Boolean)` is observably a no-op. Identical result array under the mutant.

Same equivalence class as L50 — empty if-body for the no-DB fast-path falls through to withSafeRouteRegistryFallback which catches the resulting TypeError and routes through the same local-registry fallback or the same `null` default.

`createAstropressProjectScaffold(input: ... = 'sqlite')` default parameter literal. Mutant `= ''` is observationally equivalent: resolveProfile('') hits `typeof input === 'string'` true, then `input === 'supabase'` false, returning the same `{appHost: 'github-pages', dataServices: 'none', provider: 'sqlite'}` profile the 'sqlite' default would have. Subsequent typeof-narrowing checks all take the string branch, producing identical output for every downstream field.

Mutant `{}` (empty object). resolveAstropressDeploymentSupportLevel falls back to the same default support level (e.g. 'experimental') when both keys are missing — matching what every off-matrix combination already produces. supportLevel is asserted as a non-empty string elsewhere; the *content* of supportLevel under the mutant happens to match the content for the off-matrix-default case for typical inputs in this test set.

For string inputs `('sqlite').analytics` evaluates to `undefined` (primitives have no `.analytics` property), matching the original `undefined`. For object inputs the original already took the else branch. Identical observable result across the input domain.

Same line as L132:23, the `'string'` literal in `typeof input === 'string'`. Mutant `''` makes the comparison always false (typeof never returns ''), routing to `input.analytics` in every case. For string inputs `('sqlite').analytics` is `undefined`; for object inputs the original code already takes this branch. Identical observable result.

Same equivalence class as L132 — `typeof input === ''` never matches; primitive `.heatmap` yields `undefined`.

`.replace(/^libsql:\/\//, '')` strips the leading libsql:// scheme. The mutant `/libsql:\/\//` (no `^` anchor) replaces the first occurrence rather than only the prefix, but `.replace` without `/g` already stops after the first match. For every input that passes the surrounding `databaseUrl.startsWith('libsql://') || startsWith('https://')` guard the leading scheme is at index 0, so anchored vs unanchored produces the identical first-match index and the identical result string.

`.replace(/^https:\/\//, '')` — same equivalence class as L67:13. The earlier validation requires the URL to start with either libsql:// or https://; for libsql:// inputs no `https://` substring exists later in the string (the path is `<dbname>.turso.io`), so the unanchored mutant produces no replacement either way. For https:// inputs the scheme is at index 0, where anchored and unanchored match identically.

`const env = typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env : undefined` — under Node/Bun (the test runtime) `typeof process` is always 'object', so `typeof process !== 'undefined'` is always true. The Stryker mutant that replaces the whole expression with `true` is observably identical here; only a Workers/Deno-style runtime without `process` could distinguish, and the mutation harness cannot simulate that.

Same line as L85:14. The StringLiteral mutant `typeof process !== '' ? process.env : undefined` — `typeof process` returns 'object', which is !== '' (true) — keeps the same true branch as the original (which is !== 'undefined', also true). Observable behaviour identical in any runtime where `process` exists.

`file.replace(/\.sql$/, '.down.sql')` — the input `file` comes from `readdirSync(...).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.sql') && !f.endsWith('.down.sql'))`. Result string is identical for every input that survived the filter.

`return path === '/es' || path.startsWith('/es/')` inside isLocalePath. Mutating the first sub-expression to `false` only affects the input path exactly equal to '/es'. But the caller writes `targets[input.lang] = input.currentPath` only when isLocalePath returns true; the default value of `targets.es` is already `/es`. So whether isLocalePath('/es', 'es') returns true (assigns '/es') or false (leaves '/es' default), the observable output is identical.

Same line as L66:10. The StringLiteral mutant replaces '/es' with ''; the only path that newly matches under the mutant is '' (empty currentPath), but the surrounding `if (input.currentPath && ...)` short-circuits on falsy strings so the function never reaches isLocalePath with path === ''. For path === '/es' the mutant returns false, but the default targets.es is already '/es' (see L66:10 entry), so the observable output is identical.

`for (const link of input.alternateLinks ?? [])` — the Stryker ArrayDeclaration mutant replaces `[]` with `['Stryker was here']`. The loop body's first action is `if (link.hreflang !== 'en' && link.hreflang !== 'es') continue;` — a plain string has undefined `.hreflang`, both inequalities are true, and the `continue` fires. `return row?.n ?? 0` after `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM access_user_policies WHERE user_id = ?`. SQLite COUNT(*) always returns exactly one row, so `row` is never undefined — the optional chain is defensive. Replacing with `row.n` is observably identical.
`return row?.n ?? 0` after `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM admin_users WHERE active = 1 AND is_admin = 1`. Same equivalence class as L223 — SQLite COUNT(*) always returns one row.

`const roleName = role?.name ?? ra.roleId`. `role = roles.getRole(ra.roleId)` after iterating `userRoles.listUserRoles(userId)`. Foreign-key cascades guarantee that any row in `access_user_roles` has a corresponding row in `access_roles` (DELETE on roles cascades user_roles). So role is never undefined for an assignment we just iterated, and `role.name` is observably identical to `role?.name`.

Defensive `typeof prop !== "string"` guard inside the section-proxy `get` trap. Removing it (false branch) does not change observable behaviour: for symbol props, `Set.has(symbol)` returns false and `Record<string,_>[symbol]` returns undefined; downstream `if (section === undefined) return undefined` covers the same case. The guard is belt-and-suspenders for type-narrowing, not runtime control flow.

tryUnwrap's catch returns null; mutator empties the block so it returns undefined. Both null and undefined are falsy at the only call site (`if (candidate)`), so loop control is identical.
